key_insight: 3D coupled opto-electro-thermal simulation shows lead-free MgXS3 chalcogenide perovskites can enable high-efficiency, thermally robust solar cells when thickness, doping, and defects are optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study provides device-design guidance for scalable, non-toxic absorber architectures by quantifying how absorber composition and an Sb2S3 BSF layer affect carrier collection and performance.
method: Self-consistent optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and heat transfer under AM 1.5G illumination
Systematic sweep of absorber thickness, doping, and defect density with Sb2S3 BSF evaluation
evidence_signal: Optimized simulated devices reached 28.18% PCE for MgZrS3, 26.72% for MgTiS3, and 28.16% for MgHfS3, with corresponding VOC/JSC/FF metrics reported in the abstract.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, so real-device performance may differ due to fabrication defects, interface quality, and material stability not fully captured in the model.
paper_title: Numerical exploration on unveiling the photovoltaic potential of MgXS3(X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites
